reconcile.note: Gill explains David paid two hundred foreskins though only one hundred were required, so 2 Samuel 3:14 cites the price required rather than the number delivered.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013).

sides.snippet: David arose and went, he and his men, and killed of the Philistines two hundred men; and David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full number to the king
sides.verseText: and David arose and went, he and his men, and killed of the Philistines two hundred men; and David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full number to the king, that he might be the king's son-in-law. Saul gave him Michal his daughter as wife.

sides.snippet: Deliver me my wife Michal, whom I pledged to be married to me for one hundred foreskins of the Philistines.
sides.verseText: David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, saying, Deliver me my wife Michal, whom I pledged to be married to me for one hundred foreskins of the Philistines.
